description: We’re a team of 4–5 students excited to explore space, science, and creative problem-solving through NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We’re interested in the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge and aim to create an engaging digital storytelling experience. As beginners, we’re eager to learn, collaborate, and develop our skills in research, design, and web development.
summary: Forgotten in Space is an interactive web archive built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that documents human-made spacecraft, landers, and rovers still resting on the Moon and Mars. When deep-space missions end, their hardware stays behind—yet most people only ever hear about the initial launch or landing. We created a clean, visual storytelling site that highlights iconic off-world artifacts like the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, Surveyor 3, and the Sojourner rover. Through dedicated mission cards, archival NASA imagery, and a chronological timeline spanning 1967 to 1997, visitors can explore what was left behind and where it sits today. These objects aren't just space debris; they are historical time capsules of engineering and discovery that help future generations understand how far exploration has come.
details:
• Tech Stack Used:
    • Design & Front-End Development: Canva Websites (responsive mobile/desktop layout, navigation menu, card components, and interactive timeline styling)
    • Archival Research & Imagery: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDC), NASA Science, and NASA Image and Video Library
    • Hosting: Canva Web Hosting
  • Creativity & Impact: Instead of presenting mission logs as dense tables or technical reports, we treated off-world hardware like museum artifacts. Framing landers and rovers as historical monuments makes space history approachable for students and everyday readers, shifting the conversation from "space junk" to human heritage beyond Earth.
